title: Acoustic scattering from quantum dynamics
abstract: Scattering of sound waves propagating in a compressible fluid is linked to the quantum dynamics generated by a class of non-Hermitian Hamiltonian operators. The scattering amplitude is expressed in terms of the corresponding evolution operator. This is used to provide a new proof of the reciprocity theorem in acoustic scattering, conduct analytic low-frequency acoustic scattering calculations, and study the scattering of sound waves by a finite planar array of delta-function point scatters embedded in an infinite acoustic slab. A detailed discussion of acoustic scattering properties of a homogeneous acoustic slab including a pair of delta-function point scatters on one of its faces is provided.
summary: This theoretical work connects the physics of acoustic wave scattering in fluids to the formalism of non-Hermitian quantum mechanics. By formulating the problem using a fundamental transfer matrix, the authors derive new proofs for the reciprocity theorem and provide detailed analytic results for low-frequency scattering. This methodology is valuable for understanding wave interactions in complex, inhomogeneous media.
main_problem: The paper analyzes acoustic scattering in a compressible fluid by linking the scattering process to the dynamics governed by non-Hermitian Hamiltonian operators.
main_result: The authors provide a new proof of the reciprocity theorem in acoustic scattering and derive explicit analytic formulas for low-frequency scattering calculations.
method: The analysis uses a dynamical formulation based on the fundamental transfer matrix ($\mathbf{X}_M$) derived from the governing wave equation (Bergmann's equation).
model_or_system: The system is a compressible fluid undergoing acoustic scattering, modeled by Bergmann's equation. The scattering dynamics are mapped onto an effective non-unitary quantum system described by a Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Scattering amplitude ($f$), differential cross section ($|\mathbf{f}|^2$), and transfer matrix elements ($	ilde{U}_{\vec{p}, z, z_0}^q$).
important_parameters: Low-frequency regime ($k\ell \ll 1$), incident/scattered wave vectors ($\mathbf{k}_0, \mathbf{q}$), and the confinement length ($\ell$) of inhomogeneities.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the fundamental transfer matrix approach and assumes validity of asymptotic conditions for the scattering amplitude calculation.
figures_summary: Figures show the schematic setup for scattering and plots of the differential cross section versus scattering angle ($\vartheta$), comparing cases with and without an embedded homogeneous slab.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by relating the wave equation to quantum dynamics, deriving the scattering amplitude from the transfer matrix, proving reciprocity, and applying the method to specific geometries like point scatterers and homogeneous slabs.
why_interesting: The mathematical framework—mapping classical wave scattering to non-Hermitian quantum dynamics—is highly relevant to open quantum systems and wave propagation in structured media.
